components.name: Filepicker
components.description: The GUI for picking files

fields.description:
h3. Impact

The file picker dialog can overflow the viewport on short laptop-sized screens.  
Users may see the picker content cut off or spilling outside the dialog.

h3. Expected behaviour

The picker content should size to its content.  
The dialog should stay within the viewport, even when the folder is empty.

!image-20260726-023127.png|width=671,alt="image-20260726-023127.png"!



h3. Actual behaviour

The {{.fp-content}} area is forced to a fixed height of 452px, even in the empty state.  
This makes the content area extend past the dialog and viewport boundary.  
Part of the picker is cut off or spills out.

!image-20260726-023054.png|width=671,alt="image-20260726-023054.png"!



h3. Steps to reproduce

* Use a browser window with a short viewport height, for example a laptop screen or a window resized to about 650px usable height.
* Go to any file field, for example:
** Course administration → Edit settings → Course image
** Any Files and uploads field
* Open the file picker.
* Select Server files, or any repository.
* Navigate into an empty folder with “No files available”.

h3. Environment

* Short viewport heights, such as laptop screens.
* Browser windows resized to a short usable height.
* File picker dialogs using {{responsiveWidth: 768}}.

h3. Workarounds

No workaround was provided.

h3. Other information

{{theme/boost/scss/moodle/filemanager.scss}} (in 5.1+: {{public/theme/boost/scss/moodle/filemanager.scss}}):

{code:css}.file-picker .fp-content {
    border-top: 0;
    background: $filemanager-picker-bg;
    clear: none;
    overflow: auto;
    height: 452px;   // ← fixed height, applied even to the empty state
}{code}

Combined with the fixed, width-only-responsive dialogue in {{repository/filepicker.js}} (≈ lines 1462–1486):

{code:javascript}var width = 873;                 // fixed width
...
this.mainui = new M.core.dialogue({
    ...
    width: width + 'px',
    responsiveWidth: 768,        // responsive on width only
    height: '558px',             // fixed height, no vertical responsiveness
    ...
});{code}

There is no vertical responsiveness, so on short viewports the fixed 452px content cannot shrink and overflows.

fields.summary: Assignment grades remain editable in workflow states unavailable to the grader

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: Assignment
components.description: The new mod_assign module available since Moodle 2.3

fields.description:
h2. Background

The {{assign::grading_disabled}} and {{assign::update_grade}} methods read {{workflowstate}} from the *assign_grades* record, however it’s stored in {{assign_user_flags}}. The checks therefore do nothing, allowing graders to edit grades in workflow states they cannot manage. A similar issue was identified in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-70441).|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-70441).|smart-link] .

This issue also covers multiple marking: once the overall workflow state is “Ready for release” or “Released”, individual marker marks must not be modified, including by users with permission to manage or release the overall workflow state.

h2. Replication steps

# Create a grader role with *mod/assign:grade*, but _without_ *mod/assign:reviewgrades*, mod/*assign:releasegrades*, or *mod/assign:managegrades*
# Create an assignment with marking workflow enabled
# Have a student submit
# As a teacher or administrator, give the submission a grade and set its workflow state to “Released”
# Log in as the grader and open the student’s grading page
# Change the grade and save it

*Expected*: The grade is read only because “Released” is not a workflow state available to this grader.
*Actual*: The grade remains editable and the released grade can be changed.

For multiple marking, the expected result is individual marker marks must also be read only once the overall state is “Ready for release” or “Released”, including for users who can manage or release that state.

fields.summary: Show the visibility control on every activity card in edit mode

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

fields.description:
h2. Rationale

The availability control only appears once an activity is already hidden, so changing a visible one means opening the ⋮ menu on each card. Showing it on every card makes availability something you change in place.

It also needs a label beside the icon, so the state can be read from the card rather than inferred from an icon.

And when an activity isn't shown to students, the card should say so without being read — the icon drops its colour and the text mutes, so a teacher scanning a section can see what's live.

h2. Figma

 [https://www.figma.com/design/rlo17bSNmm9tChVnLgbJa6/MDL-87755---LMS-uplift--phase-1-?node-id=4501-47282&m=dev|https://www.figma.com/design/rlo17bSNmm9tChVnLgbJa6/MDL-87755---LMS-uplift--phase-1-?node-id=4501-47282&m=dev|smart-link] 

Working prototype to understand the interaction (not for design details) 

* [https://moodlelms.com/prototypes/PROTOTYPE-course-settings.html|https://moodlelms.com/prototypes/PROTOTYPE-course-settings.html|smart-link] 

h2. Scope

h3. *The control*

* Edit mode: 
** Renders on every activity card in edit mode, in the same position, whatever the current value.
** Labels are shown in edit mode only
* View mode:
** No changes - nothing for a shown activity, an indicator for the other two.
** Continue to only show icon, no label
* Three values for the dropdown
** Drop-down labels are new: "Available", "Hidden", "Not shown"
** These require content approval
* 28px tall, matching the control row built by [MDL-87840|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87840].
* A teacher without permission to change visibility gets a static indicator, edit mode included.

h3. *Copy changes and their mappings*

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
The changed/new copy needs content approval

* Content writer to approve all five strings before this ships.
* The Figma shows different option labels and longer descriptions. The table above is the proposal.
{panel}

||*Dropdown label (new)*||*Icon* (no change)||*Option* _within dropdown (no change)_||Description today||Description proposed||
|Available|{{fa-eye}}|Show on course page|"Available to students (subject to any access restrictions which may be set)."|"Available to students"|
|Hidden|{{fa-eye-slash}}|Hide on course page|"Not available to students."|no change|
|Not shown|{{fa-eye-low-vision}}|Make available but don't show on course page|"Available to students if you provide a link. Activities will still appear in the gradebook and other reports."|"Available to students if you provide a link"|

h3. *Accessibility*

*expand for details*

* The accessible name states the feature and the current value — "Availability: Hidden from students" — and updates when the value changes.
* The drop-down label is hidden from assistive technology so the name isn't read twice, and the name must contain the drop-down label (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name). The shown state announces "Available on course page" so that it does.
* The drop-down reports its expanded state; options report which is selected.
* Keyboard recommendations: 
** Enter, Space, Up or Down opens on the current value; Up/Down wraps; Home and End jump to first and last; Escape closes; Tab closes and moves on. Focus returns to the drop-down on every close path.
* Value changes are announced, including when the tab is in the background and when the same value is set twice.
* The view-mode indicator carries a tooltip naming the state. Use the existing core mechanism — {{data-bs-toggle="tooltip"}}, initialised by {{enableTooltips()}} in {{theme/boost/amd/src/loader.js}}, which handles hover, keyboard focus and Escape. Register the control with the dynamic-content initialiser so the tooltip survives a re-render after the value changes.
* The view-mode indicator is focusable and not disabled.

fields.description:
h2. Rationale

The group mode control is hidden until you hover the card when the mode is "no groups", and that hover requirement is only lifted below 576px. On a tablet there is no hover and no small-screen fallback, so the control can't be reached at all.

It also needs a label beside the icon, so the mode can be read from the card rather than inferred from an icon.

h2. Figma

h2. Scope

*The control*

* Renders persistently in edit mode at every width, all three options, including when the value is "no groups". No hover or focus gating.
* View mode: nothing for "no groups", a static indicator for separate or visible groups.
* Where the course forces group mode, a static indicator renders and the control isn't editable.
* Where the module doesn't support groups, nothing renders in either mode.
* In Edit mode: The drop-down label sits beside the icon (English strings: "No groups", "Separate", "Visible" ) which changes with the value. E
* In view-mode: The indicator stays icon-only. Same treatment as [MDL-89320|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89320], which sits beside it on the card, so the two must match.

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}

* Drop-down labels are new: "No groups", "Separate", "Visible". These are the only new strings.
* Content writer to approve the three drop-down labels before this ships.

*Accessibility requirements*

h3. Accessibility
* The accessible name states the feature and current value — "Group mode: Separate groups" — and updates when the value changes.
* The drop-down label is hidden from assistive technology so the name isn't read twice, and the name must contain the drop-down label (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name). All three hold against the core strings.
* The drop-down reports its expanded state; options report which is selected.
* Keyboard: Enter, Space, Up or Down opens on the current value; Up/Down wraps; Home and End jump to first and last; Escape closes; Tab closes and moves on. Focus returns to the drop-down on every close path.
* Value changes are announced, including when the tab is in the background.
* The view-mode indicator carries a tooltip naming the mode. Use the existing core mechanism — {{data-bs-toggle="tooltip"}}, initialised by {{enableTooltips()}} in {{theme/boost/amd/src/loader.js}}, which handles hover, keyboard focus and Escape. Register the control with the dynamic-content initialiser so the tooltip survives a re-render after the value changes.
* The view-mode indicator is focusable and not disabled.

* The select-all reports its partial state and what it selects.

And the student can see the feedback of each marker, along with the overall (general) feedback.

Since this change affects students, we would like to support the students part in the Moodle app, so students can also see the feedback for each marker in there. However, the WebServices weren’t modified as part of this issue, so right now there’s no way to obtain that information via WebService.

The WebService that currently returns the feedback is {{mod_assign_get_submission_status}}. In an assign with multiple markers, it’s only returning the overall/generic feedback, but not the feedback for each marker. We should probably modify the WebService to also return the feedback for each marker (when the user calling the WebService is allowed to see this information).

The course controls are easily visible to the user

The course controls require the user to horizontally scroll, which makes it easy to miss in a long list of courses.

fields.summary: Lesson "Skip navigation" link does not bypass the menu (duplicate maincontent id)

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description: Follow-up to MDL-84065, raised by Matt Porritt during peer review of that issue. h2. Summary When the Lesson left menu is shown, the Lesson renders its own hand-rolled "Skip navigation" link. It does not work: it points at {{#maincontent}}, but that id collides with the core "Skip to main content" target, so the link lands _before_ the menu instead of after it, and its intended target is not focusable anyway. MDL-84065 did not touch this because Lesson does not use {{core_renderer::skip_link_target()}}. h2. Problem With the Lesson left menu enabled there are two elements with {{id="maincontent"}} on the page: # The core activity header target ({{}}), rendered by {{$OUTPUT->header()}} at the top of the page, before the menu. Since MDL-84065 this one is focusable. # The Lesson's own anchor, rendered after the menu, just before the lesson content: {code:php}// public/mod/lesson/view.php:262 and public/mod/lesson/continue.php:91 echo '';{code} The Lesson "Skip navigation" link targets that same id: {code:php}// public/mod/lesson/locallib.php:542 $content = '' . get_string('skip', 'lesson') . ... // "Skip navigation"{code} Because a fragment resolves to the first matching id in the document, {{#maincontent}} resolves to the core header target (item 1), which is _before_ the menu in the DOM. So activating "Skip navigation" moves to a point before the menu, and the next Tab goes straight back into the menu. The Lesson's own anchor (item 2), which is correctly placed after the menu, is never reached and is not focusable either (an {{}} with no {{href}} and no {{tabindex}}). Net effect: the "Skip navigation" link fails to bypass the menu for all keyboard users, and the duplicate id is invalid HTML. The link also uses {{class="accesshide"}}, so it is not visible when focused (WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible, Level AA). h2. Steps to reproduce # Create a Lesson, set "Display left menu" on, and add a content page (branch table) that shows in the menu, so the left menu is displayed. # View the lesson and Tab to the "Skip navigation" link (top of the menu), then activate it. # Note that focus does not land after the menu; tabbing onward re-enters the menu. Quick check in the browser console: {{document.querySelectorAll('[id="maincontent"]').length}} returns 2 (duplicate id), and activating the "Skip navigation" link leaves {{document.activeElement}} before the menu rather than on the lesson content. h2. Root cause Three problems compound: # Duplicate id: the Lesson target reuses {{maincontent}}, which collides with the core header target, so the link resolves to the wrong element (before the menu). # The Lesson target is not focusable (bare {{}}, no {{href}}/{{tabindex}}). # The Lesson does this with a hand-rolled anchor instead of {{core_renderer::skip_link_target()}}, so it did not benefit from MDL-84065. h2. Suggested fix Give the Lesson skip link its own unique, focusable target after the menu, and point the link at it: * {{view.php}} and {{continue.php}}: replace the anchor with a unique, focusable target {{}} (id no longer collides with core {{maincontent}}). * {{locallib.php}}: point the skip link at {{#lessoncontent}}, and change its class from {{accesshide}} to {{visually-hidden-focusable}} so it is visible on focus (addresses the 2.4.7 point too). After the fix: a single {{#maincontent}} remains (core), the Lesson has its own {{#lessoncontent}} target after the menu, activating "Skip navigation" moves focus past the menu, and the link is visible on focus. An alternative to the hand-rolled target is to route through {{core_renderer::skip_link_target()}} with a unique id, which removes the duplication. h2. Testing notes Enable the Lesson left menu, then verify: only one {{#maincontent}} exists; activating "Skip navigation" moves focus to the lesson content after the menu (check with a screen reader, or via {{document.activeElement}} in the console); and the "Skip navigation" link is visible when focused. Cover both the lesson view page and the continue page, since both render the target.

fields.description:
Notify a user when one of their personal access tokens is nearing its expiry date, so they can create a replacement before it stops working. This covers the notification only — creation, display, and deletion of tokens is handled in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89185|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89185|smart-link].

Notification channels:

* Email, sent to the user's account email address.
* A Moodle notification, delivered through the standard notification system (so it also respects the user's notification preferences, e.g. email digest settings, and appears in the notification bell/list).

Notification content should include the token's name, its expiry date, and a link to the personal access token management page so the user can act on it directly.

Open questions to resolve before/during design:

* How far ahead of expiry should the first (and any repeat) reminder be sent — e.g. 7 days, with a possible second reminder at 1 day?
* Should this be a one-time reminder or repeat until the token is renewed/deleted or actually expires?
* Should there be a separate notification when the token actually expires, distinct from the "about to expire" warning?
* Should users be able to opt out of this notification type, consistent with Moodle's general notification preference model?

*Acceptance criteria:*

* Users receive an email and a Moodle notification before a personal access token expires.
* The notification identifies the specific token and links to the management page.
* Notification timing and repeat behaviour are defined and documented.
* Notification preferences follow Moodle's standard notification framework where applicable.

fields.summary: TinyMCE Premium: get_api_key always returns usecloud=true regardless of the self-hosted plugin source setting

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: Text editor TinyMCE
components.description: The default text editor in Moodle 4.2 onwards

fields.description:
h4. Problem statement

{{tiny_premium\external\get_api_key::execute()}} determines whether Tiny Premium plugins should be loaded from Tiny Cloud or from the self-hosted package based on the {{tiny_premium/plugin_source}} admin setting.

The comparison used to make this decision is incorrect, causing self-hosted sites to always fall back to loading premium plugins from Tiny Cloud regardless of the configured plugin source.

h4. Current behaviour

* {{get_api_key.php}} compares {{get_config('tiny_premium', 'plugin_source')}} with {{manager::PACKAGE_SELF_HOSTED}} using a strict {{!==}} comparison.
* {{get_config()}} returns configuration values as strings, while {{manager::PACKAGE_SELF_HOSTED}} is an integer.
* As a result, the strict comparison always evaluates to {{true}}, so {{usecloud}} is always set to {{true}}.
* Therefore, setting *Plugin source* to *Self-hosted* has no effect. Premium plugins are still loaded from Tiny Cloud, including the associated CDN requests.

h4. Steps to reproduce

# Configure {{tiny_premium/plugin_source}} to *Self-hosted*, with a valid self-hosted path configured for the base TinyMCE package.
# Enable a premium plugin, for example Markdown, and load the editor.
# Open the browser network tab and observe that the premium plugin script is requested from {{cdn.tiny.cloud}} instead of the configured self-hosted path.

h4. Expected behaviour

When {{plugin_source}} is set to *Self-hosted*, {{usecloud}} should evaluate to {{false}}, and the premium plugins should be loaded from the local self-hosted files instead of Tiny Cloud.

h4. Root cause

This is a type mismatch: a string returned by {{get_config()}} is being compared to an integer constant using {{!==}}.

h4. Fix

Cast the configuration value to an integer before performing the comparison:

{code:javascript}'usecloud' => (int) get_config('tiny_premium', 'plugin_source') !== manager::PACKAGE_SELF_HOSTED,{code}

The fix has already been applied on {{main}} as part of [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88547|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88547|smart-link].

This ticket is only to backport the same fix to the *5.1 and 5.2*, which include the self-hosted Tiny Premium support introduced by [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-85727|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-85727|smart-link]

fields.summary: Pressing Escape on an open help popover inside a modal closes the whole modal

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: JavaScript
components.description: Anything related to Javascript infrastructure. Specific JS scripts should be handled by the component that the code is in.

fields.description:
When a help popover is open inside a modal dialogue, pressing {{Escape}} closes the entire modal rather than just the popover. Where the modal is configured with {{removeOnClose}}, it is destroyed rather than hidden, so any work in progress is lost without confirmation.

Any Moodle modal containing a help icon is affected, not only the TinyMCE image dialogue used in the steps below.

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as an admin and open your profile in edit mode.
# In the Description editor toolbar, click the *Image* button.
# Click *Browse repositories* and upload any image. The *Image details* dialogue appears.
# Type something into *How would you describe this image to someone who cannot see it?*
# Click, or Tab to, the help button beside the *Decorative image* checkbox. The help popover opens.
# Press {{Escape}}.

h2. Expected behaviour

Only the help popover closes. The Image details dialogue stays open with the uploaded image and the alternative text intact. A second {{Escape}} then closes the dialogue.

This is the principle already accepted in MDL-44079, "Pressing escape in nested modal dialogues should only close the top dialogue": the innermost open overlay should consume the key.

h2. Actual behaviour

The whole Image details dialogue closes on the first {{Escape}}. Because {{tiny_media}}'s image modal sets {{removeOnClose}}, the dialogue is destroyed rather than hidden, so the uploaded image and the alternative text are lost with no confirmation.

h2. Root cause

Two keydown handlers are involved, bound at different levels of the DOM:

* {{core/modal}} binds Escape to the *modal root element*, an ancestor of the help button: {{lib/amd/src/modal.js:1052}}.
* {{theme_boost/loader}} binds its help popover Escape handling to {{document}}: {{theme/boost/amd/src/loader.js:120}}.

The event bubbles target → modal root → document, so the modal's handler runs *first* and closes the dialogue. The popover hide then runs against an already closed modal.

Because {{ImageModal}} sets {{modalConfig.removeOnClose = true}} ({{lib/editor/tiny/plugins/media/amd/src/image/imagemodal.js:42}}), {{modal.js:1058}} takes the {{destroy()}} branch rather than {{hide()}}, which is why the form state is not recoverable.

h2. Note for whoever fixes this

Adding {{e.stopPropagation()}} to the loader's existing document level handler *will not work*, because it runs after the modal has already handled the key. The fix has to intercept earlier:

# Handle Escape for help popovers in the *capture phase* at document level, or bind the handler *on the trigger element* itself, and stop propagation only when a popover is actually shown.
# Or teach {{core/modal}} to ignore Escape while a popover or tooltip inside it is open. This is more general, since any Bootstrap popover or tooltip in any Moodle modal has the same problem, not just help buttons.

Option 2 covers the whole class of bug.

Whichever route is taken, Escape must only be consumed when a popover is genuinely open, otherwise Escape stops closing modals whenever a help button merely has focus, which would be its own regression.

h2. Accessibility framing

Potentially fails *WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA)* on its *Dismissible* requirement, which asks for a way to dismiss focus-triggered additional content _without moving keyboard focus_. The popover is focus-triggered ({{theme/boost/amd/src/loader.js:191}}) and obscures other content, so the criterion's exceptions do not apply. Escape is the only dismissal that does not move focus, and inside a modal it destroys the dialogue. Tab works but moves focus, which the criterion excludes.

Caveat for review: a strict reading could say the content _is_ dismissed without moving focus, so only the side effect is at fault. This is also specific to modals. On an ordinary page Escape dismisses the popover cleanly.

Also relevant: *3.3.4 Error Prevention (AA)* where the modal's form modifies stored data or submits test responses, and *2.4.3 Focus Order (A)* as a consequence, since focus is lost to the body rather than returning somewhere sensible.

Not claimed, in case an automated checker suggests them: *3.2.1 On Focus* and *3.2.2 On Input* need the change to come from focus receipt or a setting change, not a keypress; *3.2.4 Consistent Identification* is about naming, not key behaviour; *2.1.1 Keyboard* is met, since Tab dismisses the popover; *3.2.5 Change on Request* fits best conceptually but is AAA.

The expected behaviour comes from the ARIA APG rather than WCAG: Escape closes the innermost overlay.

h2. Verification note

Observed on main (5.3dev) while testing MDL-63567. The affects versions were set from code inspection as well: neither {{lib/amd/src/modal.js}} nor the Escape handling in {{theme/boost/amd/src/loader.js}} differs on 5.1 and 5.2. *4.5 is very likely affected too* and should be added if someone can confirm the behaviour there, but it was not reproduced by hand on each stable branch, so please adjust the affects versions if you would rather only list what has been reproduced.

h2. Related issues

* MDL-44079: the same principle for nested modal dialogues. Closed.
* MDL-82570: introduced Escape handling for help popovers.
* MDL-83741: a later regression in the same popover trigger handling, which suggests this area benefits from Behat coverage alongside any fix.
* MDL-77208: added the manual trigger and Tab handling that the current Escape handler sits in.

fields.summary: MDL-88407 multiplicator/offset assignment grading fix does not freeze grades

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: Assignment
components.description: The new mod_assign module available since Moodle 2.3

fields.description:
When [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88407|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88407|smart-link] was applied, it unintentionally missed our [process to freeze affected grades|https://docs.moodle.org/dev/How_to_fix_gradebook_issues].

We need to freeze existing grades in line with that process, because there are ways for a re-grade to be triggered automatically, for example by adding a new grade item. Below is a video of that example, showing the grade change once a grade item is added.

*Video example:*

[^Regrade-2026-08-17 17-12-55.mkv]



Root cause (SS updated this for further review and development work): *Anyone reviewing should read this.*

The gradebook stores two numbers for each grade: {{rawgrade}} (the original mark from the activity, for example 50/100 from an assignment) and {{finalgrade}} (what appears in the gradebook after applying the grade item's multiplicator/offset and any penalty).

*Before MDL-88407*, the penalty code did things in the wrong order. When a penalty was deducted, it took the final grade (which already had the multiplicator applied), subtracted the penalty, and wrote the result back into {{rawgrade}}. The gradebook then applied the multiplicator _again_ to compute finalgrade. With multiplicator 1.1, a mark of 50 with a 10-point late penalty was stored as {{rawgrade = 45}} (that is 50×1.1 − 10, a value that already contains the multiplicator) and displayed as 49.5 (45×1.1, multiplicator applied twice). MDL-88407 fixed the formula, {{rawgrade}} now always keeps the original mark (50), the penalty is subtracted from the raw mark, and factors are applied once: finalgrade = (50 − 10) × 1.1 = 44.

*The regression*: the fix changed the formula but did nothing to address the already-stored corrupted rows and did not freeze the affected courses. Moodle's standard process for calculation-changing fixes ("gradebook freeze") requires that existing grades stay untouched until a teacher explicitly accepts the change. Without the freeze, the moment anything triggers a regrade (adding a grade item, changing course settings, etc.), the _new_ formula is applied to the _old corrupted_ {{rawgrade}}: (45 − 10) × 1.1 = 38.5. The student's visible grade changes silently from 49.5 to 38.5, and it's wrong in both worlds: neither the old value (49.5) nor the truly correct one (44).

fields.summary: Course view (bulk edit mode): checkboxes overlap activities, subsection misaligned, and section/subsection divider touches first activity

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
Follow-up to MDL-87805 (structural-grey depth/elevation redesign). These issues only appear in *course view, bulk edit mode* — i.e. Edit mode → Bulk actions enabled — not in default edit mode and not in view mode.

*Steps to reproduce*

# Go to a course as a user with editing capabilities.
# Turn editing on.
# Enable "Bulk edit" mode.
# Observe the section/subsection/activity layout.

!image-20260826-053445.png|width=739,alt="image-20260826-053445.png"!



*Issue 1 — Checkboxes overlapping activity content*

The bulk-selection checkboxes no longer align properly; some overlap with their activity's content instead of sitting cleanly beside it. Originally flagged in [this coment|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87805?focusedCommentId=1158699].

*Issue 2 — Subsection card misaligned*

The *subsection* name/header sits slightly to the left compared to the other activities in the section. Before the MDL-87805 patch it aligned with the checkbox column; now it doesn't align with anything. It should be aligned with the other activities instead.

*Issue 3 — Section/subsection divider touching the first activity*

The horizontal divider/border under both the section header and the subsection header sits flush against the top border of the first activity below it, with no gap. A small gap should be added.

*Expected:* Checkboxes don't overlap content, subsection header aligns with activities, and there's a visible gap between the divider and the first activity — in bulk edit mode.
*Actual:* All three issues reproduce, only in bulk edit mode.
